pr_body:
There were 4 classes of failure:

- line ending problems;
- unicode problems;
- file path munging problems; and
- a "hang" in test_cmp_http.

The unicode problems appear to be somewhere between wine or msys - they
don't actually appear to be a problem with the built binaries. We just skip
those tests for now.

Fixes #13558

issue_context.title: mingw character set issues?
issue_context.body:
The log at https://travis-ci.com/github/openssl/openssl/jobs/450013652 contains weird characters and failing tests:
```
C=US, ST=CA, L=San Francisco, O=Example Company, OU=Example Company Unit, CN=Alice Ascii Domain
error 63 at 0 depth lookup: email address mismatch
error ../../test/recipes/25-test_eai_data/ascii_leaf.pem: verification failed
wine ../../apps/openssl.exe verify -nameopt utf8 -no_check_time -verify_email 学生@elementary.school.example.com -CAfile ../../test/recipes/25-test_eai_data/ascii_chain.pem ../../test/recipes/25-test_eai_data/ascii_leaf.pem => 2
not ok 6
```

Note the "学生@elementary.school.example.com"

In the same log file:
```
Could not read certificate from ../../test/shibboleth.pfx
42000000:error:16000071:STORE routines:try_pkcs12:error verifying pkcs12 mac:crypto/store/store_result.c:564:
Unable to load certificate
wine ../../apps/openssl.exe x509 -text -in ../../test/shibboleth.pfx -out out.pem -passin 'pass:σύνθημα γνώρισμα' => 1
not ok 6
```

It's the 64 bit target with those messages, the 32 bit target doesn't have those errors.
comments: Hmmm, since this is mingw, it might involve the magic environment variable that has libcrypto convert from the current windows codepage to utf-8.

review_comments: I wonder if this is related to gmtime() using a static buffer which is overwritten.
It's unclear, but as a single threaded app this shouldn't make a difference.
More along the lines of something in mktime overwriting the gmtime buffer.

Seems likely. Microsoft's documentation even notes:
> Note that gmtime and localtime (and _gmtime32, _gmtime64, _localtime32, and _localtime64) use a single buffer per thread for the conversion. If you supply this buffer to mktime, _mktime32 or _mktime64, the previous contents are destroyed.

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/mktime-mktime32-mktime64?view=msvc-160

While this doesn't say that you can't pass the buffer to `mktime` (which suggests it's allowed), it does say that the Windows `mktime` touches the buffer. Perhaps the Windows or Visual Studio `mktime` internally makes a copy to account for this, but the Wine or MinGW doesn't?
